stories.title: President, PM agree on resolving 'all matters' through dialogue amid rising political temperatures
summary: The meeting follows recent hard-hitting remarks by President Zardari’s son, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, who questioned past decisions and actions taken by the ruling coalition — steered by PML-N and supported by PPP.

Despite months having passed since the debate began, Bilawal claimed that no one from the government had brought up the matter with him or President Zardari, even though some federal ministers have voiced their support for more provinces.
He also voiced his strong opposition to a referendum on creating new provinces — as initially suggested by Naqvi and endorsed by Information Minister Attaullah Tarar in response to Bilawal’s speech.

stories.title: Silicon Valley elites 'bankrolled' news platform Visegrad24 publishing pro-Israel content: report
summary: An extensive investigation by American magazine Wired revealed on Thursday how an “anti-migrant, pro-Israel propaganda machine” took form and gained traction via bankrolling by Silicon Valley elites.

Tompson here admitted that his “goal is to fundraise off of this”, the report added, noting that he succeeded according to “an extensive trove of V24 financial records, internal communications, screenshots from group chats, and correspondence with donors”.
According to the report, messages to the colleague in November 2023 revealed that Tompson was added to two groups “that actively push back against founders who have supported Palestine”.

stories.title: NCCIA claims uncovering network allegedly involved in up to Rs1tr betting, money laundering
summary: Billions in suspicious transactions unearthed According to NCCIA, a detailed financial analysis revealed exceptionally high transaction volumes in accounts allegedly associated with the network: Rs.

Banking officials, company directors under probe The investigation has brought suspected banking officials, company directors, business operators, payment facilitators and account holders under scrutiny.
NCCIA Karachi conducted coordinated raids at multiple premises and arrested several individuals allegedly involved in the network.

stories.title: US, China, Russia sign ‘peace declaration’ after historic Trump, Xi, Putin meeting
summary: Trump had insisted nuclear arms control be a central topic of the summit. “It’s not an easy thing to do, give them up,” Trump told Xi and Putin as the meeting began.
Differences over Ukraine, Iran and trade Earlier on Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”.

Chinese President Xi Jinping welcomes U.S. President Donald Trump upon his arrival at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting on November 18, 2026 in Shenzhen, China.

stories.title: Pakistan, Qatar reaffirm commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in security, counter-terrorism: ISPR
summary: Pakistan and Qatar reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in the areas of institutional cooperation, security and counter-terrorism on Thursday, the military’s media affairs wing said.

He also conveyed Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani’s congratulatory messages and best wishes to the prime minister. “He appreciated Pakistan’s role and efforts for promoting peace and stability in the region,” the statement added.

The two also agreed to enhance cooperation between Qatar’s National Cyber Security Agency and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. “A decision was made to improve coordination between the two interior ministries to enhance bilateral cooperation,” the statement said.

stories.title: UN rights chief calls for Imran Khan’s release, urges political de-escalation
summary: United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk on Thursday called for the release of former prime minister Imran Khan, urging Pakistani authorities to ensure his proper treatment and take steps to ease political tensions surrounding his detention.

The persistent denial of adequate health care, family visits, and regular meetings with legal counsel to former Prime Minister Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi, his wife, during their detention is a violation of Pakistan’s international human rights obligations.

Also Read: Imran Khan's open letter to CJs shocks opposition “By denying Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi their rights, the Pakistani authorities are violating their obligations under international law,” Amnesty said in its statement.

stories.title: 'Giving students hope for a better future': Schools in Pakistan, UK, Nigeria among winners in global prizes
summary: Schools in Britain, Nigeria, Brazil, Pakistan and South Korea were named winners of the World’s Best School Prizes on Thursday for work including supporting student well-being, helping underserved communities and coordinating support for children with complex learning needs.

Public primary school Escola Municipal GET IV Centenario won the Overcoming Adversity prize for its hands-on learning model focused on creativity, emotional development and student leadership, serving 261 students.

A separate prize decided by public vote, the Community Choice award, went to Darussafaka Egitim Kurumlari, a full-scholarship boarding school in Istanbul, for a two-track model that includes remote learning for children affected by earthquakes.

stories.title: FCC sets aside high court rulings upholding infrastructure cess in Sindh, KP
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) on Thursday set aside high court rulings upholding the infrastructure cess imposed by the Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments.
A provincial levy imposing an additional fiscal burden on imported or exported goods and operating through the customs-clearance mechanism directly engaged the federal legislative domain, he said.
The counsel further argued that a provincial legislature could not acquire legislative competence over a federal subject merely by describing a customs-linked fiscal levy as an infrastructure cess.

stories.title: Turkish energy minister arrives in Karachi ahead of Oruç Reis offshore exploration mission
summary: According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Energy on X, Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik welcomed Bayraktar and his delegation upon their arrival, alongside Petroleum Secretary Hamed Yaqoob Sheikh and Sindh Minister Syed Zulfiqar Ali Shah.

Earlier this month, the Petroleum Division announced that the Turkish research vessel would arrive in Karachi between Nov 17 and 20 to begin offshore exploration, describing the development as Pakistan's first major push to revive such activities in two decades.
"Its arrival will revive Pakistan's offshore exploration efforts after 20 years, marking a new milestone in Pakistan-Türkiye energy cooperation," the division said in a statement.

stories.title: DPM Dar, Asean secretary general agree to enhance cooperation to address ‘non-traditional’ security challenges
summary: During the talks, DPM Dar stressed the scope for closer links between the business communities of Pakistan and Asean member states as well as the significance of scholarships, student exchanges, and joint research to strengthen people-to-people ties.

Hourn “reaffirmed Asean’s commitment to strengthening relations with Pakistan, welcomed Pakistan’s interest in closer engagement, and expressed confidence that continued cooperation and the visit would help advance the partnership”, the FO added.
Last year, seven Asean member countries held a joint meeting with Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh to explore new avenues of investment and economic cooperation with Pakistan.

stories.title: Musk says he felt 'pretty foolish' about scale of midterm spending after Republican rout
summary: Elon Musk said on Wednesday he felt "pretty foolish" about the amount ​of money he spent on this year's US midterm ‌elections after Republicans suffered sweeping losses.
"I feel ​pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing ‌much ⁠for it," Musk said, speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday.
Turning to ​his own ⁠AI ambitions, Musk said Anthropic was "extremely likely" to continue renting computing capacity from SpaceX and wanted significantly more.

stories.title: Airspace ban on Indian aircraft extended till Dec 24
summary: Pakistan has extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft until Dec 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA).

The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Nov 24. “Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said.

On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass announced a series of measures, including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country.

stories.title: Pakistan, 14 other countries welcome UK, Australia sanctions on Israeli 'settlement activities'
summary: Pakistan, along with 14 other countries, on Thursday welcomed the decision of the United Kingdom and Australia to impose sanctions on companies involved in abetting "Israeli settlement activities", including through settlement construction in the West Bank.

The UK said on Tuesday it would impose sanctions on eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, as part of its effort to protect the idea of a two-state solution.

Australia on Wednesday imposed targeted sanctions on three individuals and four organisations involved in "illegal settlement expansion and human rights abuses against Palestinians" in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Denmark ratifies Trump deal over Greenland, hoping to end conflict
summary: Denmark's parliament unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States on Greenland ‌on Thursday, hoping to end a standoff over the Arctic island's future that has rattled transatlantic relations.

"This agreement modernises the ​United States-Denmark-Greenland defence partnership and bolsters the national security of the United States and our allies in NATO," ​US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement posted on X.

The signatories will now start work on a new Greenland law to screen outside investors on security grounds and plans for two new US military bases, as outlined in the agreement, Denmark’s Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus told Reuters.

stories.title: Countries weigh banning smart glasses over privacy concerns
summary: Australia The federal government said in September it was considering barring the use of camera-equipped smart glasses in government workplaces ​due to privacy and security concerns.
Britain Courts in England and Wales have prohibited the use of ​Meta smart glasses because of restrictions on taking images and videos in courts.
Norway's capital Oslo ​banned smart ⁠glasses in schools in August.

stories.title: Top UN court finds Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against Muslim Rohingya
summary: The highest United Nations court ruled on Thursday that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Rohingya Muslim minority population in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide.
The decision by the International Court of Justice, or World Court, is expected to have repercussions far beyond Myanmar, including for South Africa’s 2023 case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza.

A panel of 15 judges said “the only reasonable inference that can explain Myanmar’s actions is an intention to destroy a substantial part of the protected group namely the Rohingya population in Northern Rakhine state,” meeting the legal threshold for genocide.

stories.title: EY-led consortium signs financial advisory pact for outsourcing of Karachi, Lahore airports
summary: The Privatisation Commission and a consortium led by Ernst & Young (EY) Middle East on Thursday signed a financial advisory services agreement (Fasa) for the outsourcing of Karachi and Lahore airports.
In August, the commission had approved the appointment of a financial adviser for the outsourcing of both airports, mentioning a “consortium led by EY-Parthenon as the top-ranked interested party”.
In December 2022, the government, under the premiership of Shehbaz Sharif, decided to outsource the management of the Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad airports under a public-private partnership.

stories.title: Pakistan inch closer to victory in second Test despite Sri Lanka fightback
summary: Sri Lanka mounted a determined rearguard to stave off an innings defeat and frustrate Pakistan on the third day of the second and final Test, reaching 309-9 at stumps at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.
Milan Rathnayake led the resistance with an unbeaten 60, while Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha contributed half-centuries to keep Sri Lanka in the contest.
The pair added 53 for the seventh wicket, taking Sri Lanka past Pakistan’s first-innings total and into the lead.

stories.title: EY-led consortium to advise on outsourcing of Karachi, Lahore airports
summary: Pakistan hired an Ernst & Young (EY) Middle East-led consortium to advise on the planned outsourcing of airports in Karachi and Lahore, the Privatisation Commission said on Thursday, moving forward with efforts to bring private operators into its aviation sector.

Privatisation Commission and EY Middle East Led Consortium Sign Financial Advisory Services Agreement for Outsourcing of Jinnah International Airport, Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport, Lahore.
On July 11, the Privatisation Commission Board appointed the Asian Development Bank (ADB) as financial adviser for outsourcing the operations of Islamabad International Airport.

stories.title: Lahore named ECO Tourism Capital for 2027, to host year-long cultural events
summary: LAHORE: Lahore has formally assumed the title of Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Tourism Capital for 2027, putting Punjab’s cultural heritage and tourism potential in the spotlight of regional cooperation.

Aurangzeb described the recognition as an “international endorsement” of Lahore’s historical and cultural significance, providing an opportunity to showcase Punjab’s heritage, cultural diversity and tourism potential to the world.
She said the recognition would strengthen Lahore’s position as a leading cultural destination and bring Punjab’s wider tourism potential into the international spotlight.

stories.title: MQM-P's Khalid Maqbool urges courts to take notice of Bilawal's 'bloodshed' remark
summary: Siddiqui asserted that MQM-P had been calling for the creation of new provinces across the country and never restricted their demand to just Sindh or Karachi.

Sindh govt to contact MQM-P, others on planned rallies On the other hand, Sindh Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon maintained that his PPP did not want any kind of tension, stressing that each person could hold a different opinion without “issuing edicts” on it.

On plans of the MQM-P and the Sindh Taraqqi-pasand Party (STP) holding rallies in Karachi on Nov 29, Memon said the Sindh government would contact both parties and urge them not to go ahead with their gatherings.

stories.title: Petrol hiked by Re1
summary: On November 2, the government announced that oil refineries would bear a burden of Rs15 billion per month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them with a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each.

stories.title: Google picks Bezos' Blue Origin to launch AI computing satellites in 2029
summary: Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin said on Thursday that Alphabet's Google had selected its New Glenn rocket to launch satellites for Project Suncatcher, an ​experiment aimed at running AI systems in space.
The launch, targeted for the first quarter of 2029, will ​be Google's first heavy-lift flight dedicated to Project Suncatcher and will carry several computing ​satellites aboard New Glenn.

Each satellite will carry Google's tensor processing units, the search giant's in-house chips built to run AI programs, with computing capacity roughly equal to a rack ​of servers in a conventional data center.

stories.title: PM credits economic successes to 'productive partnership' between political, military leadership
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said Pakistan’s economic achievements were the product of a “productive partnership between the military and the political hierarchy”.
He was addressing a ceremony organised by the American Business Council of Pakistan.

During his address, the premier acknowledged that the members of the American Business Council of Pakistan had contributed “immensely” in promoting Pakistan’s economic interests. “I have no doubt that you are great ambassadors for Pakistan,” he said.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz, Hafiz Naeem to meet next week to finalise fuel relief package
summary: He made the remarks after a meeting with a government delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in Islamabad.

He said government ministers had acknowledged the party's role in raising the issue, adding that consumers had received relief of Rs146 per litre on petrol and Rs242 per litre on diesel as a result of the protests.

According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on X, Dar held a follow-up meeting with a JI delegation led by Baloch to continue consultations on petroleum prices and discuss the possibility of expanding the existing fuel subsidy scheme.

stories.title: Italian court delays ruling in Meta, TikTok social media case pending government curbs
summary: A Milan court on ​Thursday put off until January 21 its decision in a case brought by a group of ‌Italian families seeking to restrict minors' access to Meta and TikTok, as the government prepares its own curbs.

The class injunctive action, ⁠a collective lawsuit filed by MOIGE, an Italian parents' association, asks the court to require the companies, ​which operate Facebook, Instagram and TikTok, to adopt stronger age-verification systems for users under 14.
MOIGE ⁠has said it wants to protect some 3.5 million Italian children aged between 7 and 14 who it says are illegally active on social media platforms.

stories.title: Rabia’s killer to walk free as family redeems him from murder in affidavit to Rawalpindi court
summary: Additional District and Sessions Judge Khurram Saleem approved the post-arrest bail of the prime suspect against property surety bonds after the deceased’s family submitted affidavits stating that they had forgiven him and did not believe he had deliberately killed Rabia.
Rabia’s mother Rakhshanda Bibi, brother Khurram Ahmed Khan, and sister Alvina Khan also appeared before the court and recorded their statements in favour of the suspect.

Rabia Ahsan lost her life in an unfortunate accident.” The defence counsel Malik Mohsin Kalyami and the Rawalpindi High Court Bar Association Additional Secretary General Saba Faraz Raja filed the bail applications and submitted the affidavits.

stories.title: Saudi FM, Makkah Defence Alliance chief discuss defence cooperation
summary: Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Makkah Defence Alliance Secretary-General Nauman Mahmood on Thursday discussed the alliance’s institutional development and efforts to strengthen defence coordination among member states.

The Mecca Defence Alliance was established under an agreement signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Makkah on August 7.

At an emergency meeting in Riyadh on Oct 5, the three countries agreed to begin implementing their collective defence commitments immediately and appointed Mahmood as the alliance’s first secretary-general for a three-year term.

stories.title: UN officials, world leaders welcome ICJ's Rohingya genocide ruling against Myanmar
summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against the Muslim Rohingya minority population in 2017, the first time it held a state responsible for genocide.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority during military operations in 2016–17.
UN Human Rights Chief @volker_turk applauds today’s landmark judgment by the @CIJ_ICJ which found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya people.

stories.title: Formation of electoral reforms committee delayed because opposition not finalising nominees: minister
summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Thursday said the formation of the Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER) had been delayed because the opposition had yet to submit its nominees.

However, PTI believes that, as in 2017, when an electoral reform process was undertaken, the government and opposition should have equal representation in the PCER to prevent one-sided decision-making.

Earlier this month, the government, taking ownership of an initiative to bring all parliamentary parties, including the opposition, to the negotiating table on electoral reforms, formally appr­oached its allies to join the proposed PCER.

stories.title: HRCP warns Punjab theatre bill could put government beyond criticism
summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) on Thursday raised alarm over the recently passed Punjab Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026, warning that the legislation would undermine artistic freedom and incite dissatisfaction towards the government by barring free speech.

In a statement issued on the social media platform X, it said, “HRCP is deeply concerned that the recently passed Punjab Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026 effectively places the government beyond satire and criticism.” HRCP is deeply concerned that the recently passed Punjab Dramatic and Theatrical Performances Bill 2026 effectively places the government beyond satire and criticism.

Prohibiting performances deemed likely to create disaffection towards the government is a gross violation of… — Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (@HRCP87) November 19, 2026 It further warned that “prohibiting performances” would likely create disaffection towards the government. “[It] is a gross violation of artistic freedom and the right to freedom of expression.” Read: Lahore's 'Mahfil' theatre sealed by Punjab government It also raised concerns over the bill's mandatory licensing requirements, government-controlled script reviews and censorship mechanisms, arguing that these provisions institutionalised state control over artistic and cultural activities through threats of fines and imprisonment. {{pdf}} It is worth noting that Article 3 of the bill states, “Prohibition of certain dramatic or theatrical performances.– No dramatic or theatrical performances shall be held which are: (a) scandalous or defamatory; or (b) likely to excite feelings of disaffection to the Government; or (c) likely to deprave and corrupt persons present at the performance; or (d) obscene or vulgar; or (e) inciting hatred or hurting religious feelings; or (f) any other performance as may be prescribed.” The HRCP announced that it would convene a consultation with artistes and other relevant stakeholders to examine the legislation's implications and discuss possible measures to safeguard artistic and cultural freedoms.

stories.title: Govt moves to break deadlock over new provinces through political dialogue
summary: Well-placed PML-N sources told The Express Tribune that the party would form a political coordination committee comprising senior leaders to engage parliamentary parties and develop a joint strategy on key national issues through consultations.

The party's central leadership is currently examining various political and constitutional matters, including the proposed creation of new provinces and administrative units, as well as the possibility of another constitutional amendment.

Also Read: MQM-P postpones Nov 29 rally for new provinces, reiterates demand for administrative division The meeting between the president and the prime minister earlier today was among several recent engagements focusing on issues dominating the political landscape.

stories.title: Anthropic set to secure $1.8 trillion valuation in strong Nasdaq debut
summary: The strong demand for Anthropic shares amid a broader tech selloff offers hope to a sector where euphoria has somewhat cooled in recent weeks.
Big payday for co-founders Although shares can be volatile in the days following a listing, Anthropic's IPO is set to create thousands of paper millionaires and a handful of billionaires.
Anthropic's breakneck growth has so ​far defied these concerns, ⁠but some investors have said they may wait for the initial euphoria to subside before buying.

stories.title: Navy’s combat capabilities significantly enhanced across all operational domains: Admiral Ashraf
summary: Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS) Admiral Naveed Ashraf on Thursday said the Pakistan Navy has significantly enhanced its combat capabilities across all operational domains.

The naval chief further said that the navy’s combat capabilities “have recently undergone significant enhancement and transformation across all operational domains aligned with contemporary and future warfare demands”.

The naval chief described the air force and navy as “brothers in arms”, with the “maritime domain as our shared operational space”. “It is here we exercise together and shall fight alongside each other to defend our motherland.

stories.title: 10 killed as Karachi-bound passenger coach, LPG bowser collide on Makran coastal highway near Ormara
summary: He added that traffic on the Makran Coastal Highway remained suspended for several hours following the accident, leaving long queues of vehicles stranded near Basol and Ormara.
In March, seven people, including a child, were killed and eight others injured in a head-on collision between two vehicles on the coastal highway.
In January, a passenger vehicle overturned on the coastal highway in Ormara, killing 10 people and leaving more than 30 others injured.

stories.title: COP31 negotiators publish revised deal draft with no mention of fossil fuels
summary: Climate negotiators stripped out any reference to ending the ​use of fossil fuels in a slimmed-down draft deal text published on Thursday, as the COP31 meeting in Antalya, ‌Turkiye, approaches its Friday deadline.

Monday's two references ​to fossil fuels and limiting their use — a topic that deeply divides nations in the negotiations every year — ⁠were removed, as was mention of a $120 billion target for finance to help developing countries adapt to climate change.

Thursday's draft deal also called ⁠for "global cooperation" to boost electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, up from around 23% now — something proponents say would slash greenhouse gas emissions by reducing fossil fuel use.

stories.title: UN could soon be leaderless as race to succeed Guterres stalls
summary: With under two months left in Antonio Guterres' term as UN secretary-general and no agreement on a successor, the world body faces a once-unthinkable possibility: it could soon have no ​leader.

The United Nations Security Council is expected to hold another secret ballot this week to pick the next UN chief, but after eight rounds of voting, the council’s five veto-wielding ‌members have not agreed on a successor.

The failure to pick a successor, analysts say, is partly the result of a long, opaque selection process built on secret ballots that exemplifies the slowness and gridlock the next secretary-general will be expected to cure.

stories.title: PM, president agree to solve all issues through dialogue after Bilawal's remarks whip up storm
summary: Responding to a question about Bilawal's criticism of government representatives, Chaudhry said the PPP chairman had often spoken about dialogue, tolerance and the right to express opinions.

Also Read: Bilawal will be responsible for any bloodshed over new provinces: Kamal Chaudhry also argued that discussions on improving governance should extend across the country rather than focus on a single province.

The comments drew the ire of the political elite, with Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah saying that Bilawal's remarks could lead to disqualification "They were fully involved in the 26th Amendment.

stories.title: Islam forecast to exceed Christianity as world's biggest religion by middle of next decade
summary: Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s biggest religion by the middle of the next decade, the Pew Research Centre projected on Wednesday.

While Christianity has ranked as humanity’s largest religion for centuries, the global Muslim population has grown much faster and is forecast to reach 2.57 billion by 2035, compared with a projected tally of 2.52bn Christians in that year, the Pew study found.

The Pew study also concluded that Pakistan’s Muslim population was expected to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461m in 2070. “The country will rise from having the second-largest Muslim population to the world’s largest,” it said.
